narration: Your carrier advertised forty-five dollars a month. Your actual bill is seventy-three. That twenty-eight dollar gap isn't a mistake — it's a strategy.
visual: Phone screen showing '$45/mo' ad next to real bill showing '$73.00 DUE'. Animated counter ticks from 45 up to 73.

narration: There are eleven separate fees hiding inside the fine print. Universal Service Fund, E911, Administrative Fee, Regulatory Recovery — none of these were in the headline price.
visual: List of five fee line items appearing one by one with dollar amounts: USF $7.49, E911 $3.50, Admin Fee $3.99, Regulatory $2.74, State Tax $5.28. Running total climbs.

narration: Here's the thing — carriers aren't lying. They legally separate the 'base plan' from fees so they can advertise the lower number. The FCC gets over 100,000 complaints about this every single year.
visual: Split comparison: left side 'ADVERTISED' with $45 label, right side 'ACTUAL' with $73 label. A red gap bar between them labeled '$28 GAP'.

narration: And it's not just you. Three hundred fifty million Americans are on wireless plans. At twenty-eight dollars a month per line, carriers collect nearly twelve billion dollars a year in fees above what they advertised.
visual: Silhouettes of people filling the frame, then a large $12B label appearing. Bar chart showing fee revenue growing year over year.

narration: The fix is simpler than you think. Prepaid carriers — Mint Mobile, Visible, US Mobile — advertise the all-in price. That exact same coverage for thirty-five dollars total, no surprises.
visual: Two phones side by side: one labeled 'BIG CARRIER $73' and one labeled 'PREPAID $35 ALL-IN'. A green checkmark appears on the prepaid phone.

narration: Twenty-eight dollars a month is three hundred thirty-six dollars a year. Over ten years, invested at eight percent, that's over five thousand dollars — just from switching your phone plan.
visual: Piggy bank SVG filling up with coins. '$336/yr' label, then '10 YEARS' label, then '$5,000+' bursting out. CTA text: 'Check your bill tonight.'
